description.en: A liquor or bar license is issued by the State Excise Department authorizing the sale, serving, or manufacture of alcoholic beverages. The licensing regime varies enormously by state — some states have complete prohibition, while others have multiple license categories (FL-I for hotels, FL-II for retail shops, FL-III for bars and restaurants, FL-IV for clubs). The license is a prerequisite for legally operating any establishment that sells or serves alcohol.

verifiedConditions.claim: The establishment must be located in a state or union territory where the sale of liquor is permitted. Bihar, Gujarat, Mizoram, Nagaland, and Lakshadweep have total or partial prohibition. Other states regulate liquor sale through their excise departments.

The premises must comply with state excise zoning regulations. Most states prohibit liquor establishments within a specified distance (typically 100-500 meters) of religious places, educational institutions, and hospitals.
The applicant must be a legal adult (typically 21 years or above in most states). Some states set the minimum age for liquor license holders at 25 years.

unverifiedEligibility: Many states require the applicant to be a resident of that state.
Criminal background verification is conducted — applicants with certain criminal records may be denied.
Corporate applicants must have the appropriate business registration (company/LLP/partnership).
Some states limit the total number of liquor licenses per area or population.
Special tourism zones or airport/railway premises may have different licensing rules.

requirements.claim: Prescribed application form from the State Excise Department. Many states now accept online applications through their excise portals.
Identity and address proof of the applicant — Aadhaar card, PAN card, voter ID, passport.
Premises ownership proof (sale deed) or lease agreement (minimum 3-5 years in most states). The premises must meet the minimum area requirements specified by the excise department.
Business registration — shop and establishment registration, GST registration, and FSSAI license (for food-serving establishments).
Fire safety NOC from the local fire department certifying that the premises meets fire safety standards.
Health/trade license from the local municipal corporation or municipality.
Police verification certificate or NOC from the local police station confirming no criminal background and verifying the premises location.
NOC from the local municipal authority or gram panchayat and, in some states, from residents/commercial establishments within a specified radius.

processInformation.claim: Submit the application form with all required documents and the license fee at the State Excise Department's office or through the online portal. The fee amount varies significantly by state and license type.

The excise department conducts document verification, premises inspection, and police verification. The inspector checks the distance from prohibited zones, premises condition, and compliance with regulations.

processInformation.appliesTo: New license applicants in some states
processInformation.claim: In some states, a public notice is issued and objections from the public are invited. A hearing may be conducted before the licensing authority if objections are received.

The Excise Commissioner or District Collector (depending on the state) approves or rejects the application. Upon approval, the license fee and annual excise duty are collected, and the license is issued.

output.claim: A liquor/bar license specifying the license type (FL-I, FL-II, FL-III, etc.), licensed premises details, permitted hours of operation, license validity period (typically one year, renewable annually), and conditions of the license. The license must be prominently displayed at the establishment.

fees.applicability: Liquor/bar license fee (varies enormously by state and type)
fees.claim: License fees vary enormously by state and license type. For example, an FL-III (bar) license in Maharashtra may cost Rs. 5-15 lakhs per year, while in Goa it may be Rs. 50,000-2 lakhs. A retail liquor shop (FL-II) license in some states is auctioned and can cost crores. Some states charge a flat fee while others use a tender/auction system.

processingTime.applicability: Liquor/bar license from application to issuance
processingTime.claim: Processing typically takes 30-90 days depending on the state, completeness of documentation, police verification timeline, and whether a public hearing is required. Renewal applications are generally processed faster than new applications.

sources.title: State Excise Department (representative: Maharashtra Excise Department)
sources.publisher: State Excise Departments, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: State excise departments regulate the manufacture, distribution, and sale of alcoholic beverages. License categories, fees, and procedures vary by state. Online application portals are available in several states.
claimsSupported: Liquor licenses are issued by state excise departments.
Multiple license categories exist for different types of establishments.
Premises must meet zoning and distance regulations.
Police verification and premises inspection are required.
License fees vary significantly by state and license type.
sources.uncertainty: This source represents one state's implementation. Other states have vastly different fee structures, license categories, and processes. Prohibition states have no liquor licensing.

limitations: This record provides a general overview. Liquor licensing varies enormously by state and license type.
Some states (Bihar, Gujarat, Mizoram, Nagaland, parts of Manipur) have total or partial prohibition and do not issue liquor licenses.
License fees can range from a few thousand to several crores depending on the state and license type.
The record uses Maharashtra as a representative example but each state has its own excise act and rules.
Auction-based licensing systems (used in some states) are not modeled in detail.
The record does not cover manufacturer/distillery licenses, which are a separate and more complex process.
Annual renewal processes and conditions for license suspension/cancellation are not covered in detail.

review.reviewReason: State-level excise policies change frequently. License fees, categories, and procedures need individual state verification.
nextReviewTrigger: State governments revising excise policies or fee structures.
